skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

version.changelog: v1.1.14 metadata fix: 确保required_env正确声明，解决元数据不一致问题

llm.summary: The skill's behavior matches its stated purpose (scanning OpenClaw sessions and writing extracted memory to Feishu), but its runtime instructions embed Feishu credentials and full conversation contents into prompts handed to the agent, creating a realistic risk of secret or data leakage—review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required environment variables (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID), and scripts all align with an extractor that reads local OpenClaw session files and writes to Feishu (multi-table/doc). Required tools (openclaw, python3, bash) are plausible for the stated task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The scripts read full local OpenClaw session files and send their contents to an OpenClaw agent for extraction; that is expected for this skill but it means user conversation data will be forwarded. More importantly, the do_extract_and_write.sh constructs a large prompt that includes explicit references to the L2 app token and other IDs (it injects $L2_APP_TOKEN, $L2_TABLE_ID, etc. into the prompt file). Embedding credentials and full session contents into a prompt handed to an agent/LLM risks exposing secrets and private conversation data to whatever model/provider the agent uses. The SKILL.md and README document the data flow (local -> AI -> Feishu), but the prompt-based credential exposure is unnecessary and risky.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external installer or remote download; this is instruction + local scripts (no install spec). That minimizes supply-chain risk. Scripts assume openclaw CLI and standard tools (python3, bash).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The required env vars are appropriate for writing to Feishu and for sending notifications. However: (1) the scripts place those tokens directly into the AI prompt text, which may leak them to model providers or logs; (2) the scripts assume workspace paths under /root/.openclaw and will read local session files—this is functionally necessary but increases exposure if the agent or system is not isolated. The number and type of env vars are proportionate, but the way they're used is hazardous.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true, doesn't request special platform privileges, and does not modify other skills' configs. It writes to workspace files (memory/.extracted_sessions, processing files) and uses /tmp locks—expected for local background jobs. Autonomous invocation is the platform default and not by itself a concern here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (scan local OpenClaw sessions, extract memories, and write them to Feishu). However, before installing: 

- Accept that conversation contents will be read and forwarded to the OpenClaw agent and ultimately stored in your Feishu workspace; do not use this on highly sensitive conversations. 
- The extraction prompt embeds your Feishu tokens/IDs in cleartext. If your OpenClaw agent uses a remote LLM provider or logs prompts, those credentials and session contents could be exposed. Confirm the agent (and its model) runs in an environment you fully trust or modify the scripts to avoid embedding secrets in prompts. 
- Prefer letting the OpenClaw tooling perform authenticated API calls using stored credentials rather than putting tokens inside prompts. If possible, change the agent invocation so the model is not given raw tokens or sensitive text. 
- Run initially in an isolated test environment with non-production data and minimal-scope Feishu credentials. Rotate tokens after testing. 
- Review/adjust file paths (scripts assume /root/.openclaw) and secure the .env file (do not commit). 

If you can accept the data flow and trust the OpenClaw agent/LLM environment (or you change the scripts to avoid prompt-level secret exposure), the skill is coherent with its purpose. Otherwise treat it as risky and avoid installing until those issues are mitigated.
